title: Transformer model predicts B-cell epitopes of Fasciola hepatica, confirmed by dot-blot
summary: deepBCE-Parasite, a Transformer model for linear B-cell epitopes, reached about 81% accuracy and AUC 0.90 in 10-fold cross-validation and independent testing, ahead of four conventional machine learning algorithms. Applied to Fasciola hepatica leucine aminopeptidase it predicted eight epitopes, and dot-blot immunoassays confirmed specific IgG binding of seven synthetic peptides to positive sera. This is a proof of concept on one antigen.
ai_technology: Transformer-based deep learning model (deepBCE-Parasite) predicting linear B-cell epitopes from peptide sequences
organization: Sichuan University of Arts and Science

evidence.tested: Independent test set (AUC 0.90) and dot-blot immunoassay of 7 of 8 predicted epitopes with positive sera.
evidence.unknown: Serum sample sizes, performance on other parasite antigens and vaccine or diagnostic utility; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts which peptides of a parasite antigen are antibody-binding epitopes.
